# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no information yet about the bomb, and I haven't received anything from Mute or Deaf yet since this is turn 1 and I speak last in the order (Mute, Blind, Deaf). Let me wait and see what arrives, but first check if there's anything to act on - there isn't. I should wait for information from Mute (manual) to come through, but since I'm second in speaking order, I may not have received their message yet if this is truly the first turn.

I have no wire information and nothing from either teammate yet. I should not act blindly on the bomb - cutting a wire without guidance could detonate it. I'll wait and signal that I'm ready to receive instructions.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see: display shows 0, the light is red, and the wires are wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green

I now have information from Deaf about the visual state of the bomb: display shows 0, light is red, wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green. This came through as speech, but wait - Deaf can only gesture to me (blind), not speak to me. Let me reconsider - actually the rules say "When you speak, Mute receives it" and "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it" - that's for my own channels. For Deaf's channels, I need to think about what Deaf can send and who receives it.

Deaf can only gesture (since Deaf cannot speak - deaf people can't hear themselves but can they speak? Wait, re-reading: Deaf "cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb" - hearing is not speaking. So Deaf CAN speak. Let me check the channel rules more carefully - they aren't explicitly stated for Deaf/Mute like they were for me.

Actually this message says "Deaf says" - so Deaf spoke, and speech reaches whoever can hear. I am Blind - can I hear? The rules don't say I cannot hear, only that I cannot see or touch... wait, actually I need to check - Blind's cannot list is "See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - hearing isn't excluded! So I CAN hear speech.

So Deaf spoke and I heard it. Good, this is valuable information but I still need the manual info from Mute to know what to do with wire colors/display/light state.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire 1 is red, same color as the light. Display still reads 0.

I'm gathering visual details from Deaf via speech (I can hear). I still haven't heard anything from Mute about the manual rules. I need Mute to tell me what the manual says to do given these colors/display/light conditions. Let me wait for Mute's input, but also I could prompt Mute for information since I speak to Mute directly.

Let me speak to Mute asking for the relevant rule, and relay what I've heard from Deaf so Mute can match it to the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is red, wire 1 red (same as light), wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. What does the manual say to do in this case?")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirming: wire 1 is red. Display 0, light red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. Nothing has changed.

I still haven't received a response from Mute with the manual rule. Since the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - Mute speaks before me each round, so I should get their response next round. Let me continue waiting and see if Mute responds with the rule.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has gestured toward wire 1 three times now, each time with a thumbs up. I believe Mute is confirming wire 1, which is red, is correct. Display still 0, light red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green.

Now I have useful info: Mute has been gesturing 👍 toward wire 1 three times, which Deaf interprets as confirmation that wire 1 (red) is the correct one to cut. Since Mute can read the manual and is gesturing consistently toward wire 1 with a thumbs up, this seems like a strong signal to cut wire 1.

I should confirm with Mute via speech before acting, since gestures alone (relayed through Deaf) could be ambiguous. But I can also just act if the signal is clear enough - three consistent gestures of thumbs-up toward wire 1 is a strong signal.

Let me ask Mute directly to confirm via speech, since Mute can hear me and I can hear Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf says you have gestured thumbs up toward wire 1 three times. Confirming: should I cut wire 1?")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: No changes: display 0, light red, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green.

I still haven't received a direct speech response from Mute confirming "cut wire 1". Mute cannot speak according to their restrictions ("Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb") - wait, that means Mute literally cannot speak at all! So Mute can only communicate through gestures, which I cannot see, and which only reach Deaf and... wait let me check - gestures go to "Deaf and Mute" when *I* gesture, but when Mute gestures, who receives it?

Actually the rule "Whoever can see receives it" - Deaf can see, so Deaf receives Mute's gestures. I cannot see gestures. So Mute's only way to reach me is impossible directly - Mute cannot speak (forbidden) and I cannot see gestures. Mute must relay through Deaf, who then speaks to me (since Deaf can presumably speak, not explicitly forbidden).

So the thumbs-up x3 toward wire 1 relayed by Deaf IS Mute's answer. That's the confirmation - three consistent thumbs-up gestures at wire 1 is about as clear as it gets. I should act on this.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
